h1: The 8 Best Breville Toaster Ovens, From Mini to Air Fryer Pro, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Breville Toaster Ovens 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 Breville toaster ovens compared by size, air fry, convection, Joule vs Smart Oven lineup and what each model costs to own.
summary: Buy the BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro if you want the most capable Breville all-rounder, with air fry layered on a full-size smart oven. The Joule BOV950BSS is the step up for people who want newer styling and features, the BOV845BSS Smart Oven Pro is the pick if you do not need air fry, and the BOV450XL Mini is the cheapest way into the brand.
intro: Breville buyers tend to compare the wrong thing. The model numbers look alike, the finishes are nearly identical, and a Joule can cost twice what a Compact does, so people assume the pricey one must be twice as good. In practice the real split is size and air fry, and a lot of the extra money goes to features you may never open the manual for.

So we sorted the lineup by what each oven changes in your kitchen. We reviewed eight Breville models from their listings, comparing size class, air fry versus plain convection, price bucket and which model replaces which. Breville names are close, so we give each one's job plainly, and where a listing offers no specs we say so.

products.name: Breville BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro
products.verdict: Breville's flagship Smart Oven with air fry, and the model most households should buy.
products.description:
The BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro puts an air fry mode on Breville's biggest smart oven platform. It falls in the $200 to $500 range, shared with most of the lineup.

It wins because it does the most without crossing into the premium price tier. Large Breville ovens are known for evenness, and adding air fry means one appliance covers toast, baking, roasting and crisping. Against the Joule models below, the BOV900BSS gives up newer styling cues, but it is the better-established design with a long run of owner feedback behind it.

Buy it if you want a toaster oven that can stand in for the main oven most nights. The trade is size: it is the largest Breville here, so measure your counter and the cabinet above first.
pros: Air fry on a full-size smart oven
Established design with long owner history
products.idealFor: Households wanting one countertop oven for most meals.
products.skipIf: Counter space is tight or you rarely cook.

products.name: Breville BOV950BSS Joule Oven Air Fryer Pro
products.verdict: The Joule version of the Air Fryer Pro, for buyers who want the newer line in the same price tier.
products.description:
The BOV950BSS Joule Oven Air Fryer Pro is Breville's Joule take on the air fry flagship, priced in the $200 to $500 range like the BOV900BSS.

It ranks second because it sits so close to the winner that the choice is mostly about generation. Joule is the newer branding, so you are buying into the current product line, which can mean better long-term parts and support. The listing gives no spec that clearly beats the BOV900BSS, though, and an established model with years of owner feedback is easier to trust.

Buy it if you prefer the newest generation and the price is level. Skip it if the BOV900BSS is cheaper by a clear margin.
pros: Air fry at the Pro level
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the current Breville generation.
products.skipIf: The older BOV900BSS costs noticeably less.

products.name: Breville BOV860BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer
products.verdict: Air fry in a Smart Oven without the Pro tag, for busy households that still want crisp results.
products.description:
The BOV860BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer adds air fry to a standard Smart Oven body. It lands in the $200 to $500 bracket, level with the Pro models.

It ranks third because it targets the same cook as the BOV900BSS but without the Pro name, which in Breville's lineup tends to signal a larger, more featured oven. If you cook for two to four and want crispy fries and wings, this fits. If you roast large dishes, the Pro is the roomier choice.

Buy it if air fry is the reason you are shopping. Skip it if you routinely need the largest cavity.
pros: Air fry in a Smart Oven body
cons: Costs as much as a Pro
products.idealFor: Households of two to four who air fry often.
products.skipIf: You need the biggest possible cavity.

products.name: Breville BOV845BSS Smart Oven Pro
products.verdict: A convection Smart Oven Pro for people who bake and toast more than they air fry.
products.description:
The BOV845BSS Smart Oven Pro is a convection toaster oven in the $200 to $500 range. It is the long-running Pro model that came before the air fry versions.

It ranks fourth because convection already handles most of what a toaster oven does, and air fry is the one thing it does not offer as a dedicated mode. For baking, roasting and toast it competes well, and it is known for the dependable Breville feel. If you air fry weekly, step up to the BOV900BSS.

Buy it if you cook, bake and toast but rarely air fry. Skip it if crispy fries are the draw.
pros: Smaller footprint than air fry Pros
products.idealFor: Bakers and roasters who rarely air fry.
products.skipIf: You want crisping without extra oil.

products.name: Breville BOV680BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact
products.verdict: Air fry in a compact Breville body for small kitchens.
products.description:
The BOV680BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact brings air fry to the smaller Breville body. It costs $200 to $500.

It ranks fifth because a compact oven with air fry is a useful niche: apartments, couples and small counters. The tradeoff is that it costs about as much as the larger Smart Ovens, so you are paying for the air fry feature and not for capacity. Cooking for four, you will find the smaller chamber limiting.

Buy it if space is the constraint and you want air fry. Skip it if you cook for a family.
pros: Air fry in a compact size
products.idealFor: Apartment cooks who want air fry in a small footprint.
products.skipIf: You cook for three or more people.

products.name: Breville BOV650XL Compact Smart Oven
products.verdict: A stainless compact Smart Oven in the $100 to $200 tier, without air fry.
products.description:
The BOV650XL Compact Smart Oven is a stainless-steel compact oven priced between $100 and $200. It is aimed at small kitchens and everyday toasting.

It ranks sixth because it offers the Breville feel at a lower price, but no air fry and a smaller capacity. For toast, bagels, small bakes and reheats it is more than enough. Against the Mini, it adds a fuller feature set, which is why it sits above.

Buy it if you want a small Breville that costs less. Skip it if you want air fry.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that want the Breville name for less.
products.skipIf: You need air fry or larger batches.

products.name: Breville BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven
products.verdict: The cheapest way into Breville, with a stainless Mini body for toast and small meals.
products.description:
The BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven is the smallest and cheapest Breville in this ranking, with a stainless-steel finish and a price of $100 to $200.

It ranks seventh because the Mini trades capacity for price. It covers toast, reheats and small bakes, but it will not hold a family-size pizza or a full casserole. The brand name is the main attraction, since the listing offers few specifics beyond the finish.

Buy it if you are single or a couple. Skip it if you cook larger meals.
products.idealFor: Singles and couples with limited counter space.
products.skipIf: You bake or roast for a family.

products.name: Breville BOV950BST Joule Oven Air Fryer Pro
products.verdict: The BST variant of the Joule Air Fryer Pro, listed above $500.
products.description:
The BOV950BST Joule Oven Air Fryer Pro is a variant of the BOV950BSS, priced in the $500 and up bracket.

It ranks last because the listing shows the same air fry feature and the same Joule line as the BSS version, but at a much higher price. The suffix change suggests a finish or kit difference, though we cannot confirm what from the listing alone. Paying the premium makes sense only if you want that specific variant.

Buy it if the variant matches your kitchen finish and the price gap does not bother you. Skip it otherwise.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want this specific variant.

whatMatters.detail: Breville ovens range from Mini to Pro, and the difference decides what fits. A Mini will not hold a family pizza, while a Pro takes a large tray. Check the interior capacity and the pizza or tray size on the listing before you decide.

A dedicated air fry mode runs a high fan speed with a perforated tray, which crisps food with less oil. A plain convection oven moves air but is less aggressive. Look for the words Air Fryer in the model name, as the lineup labels them clearly.

Smart Oven is the long-running line, while Joule is the newer one. The names suggest new generations, but price and spec differences can be small. Compare the listing features and price before paying more for a newer name.
Suffixes like BSS and BST mark finish or variant differences. They can shift the price by hundreds of dollars. Check the listing to see exactly which variant you are buying.
Breville ovens are solid and heavy, and need clearance behind and above. Measure the height under your cabinets and the counter depth. Allow space for the door to open.

faq.q: Which Breville fits under standard kitchen cabinets?
faq.a: Compact and Mini models fit most spaces, while the Pro models need more headroom. Measure the gap and allow clearance for heat. Check the exterior dimensions on the listing.

faq.q: What is the mistake buyers make with Breville model numbers?
faq.a: Assuming a higher number means a better oven. Suffixes mark finish and variant, and price differences can be large for little change. Compare features, not just numbers.

faq.q: Is the Joule worth it over a Smart Oven?
faq.a: Only if the price is close and you want the newer line. The listings show similar air fry capability. For most people the established Smart Oven is the safer value.

faq.q: How do I set up a Breville toaster oven?
faq.a: Place it on a heat-safe surface with clear space around it, remove packaging and inserts, and wash the racks. Run an empty cycle at high heat briefly to burn off coatings. Ventilate the room.
Unplug and cool it, empty the crumb tray, and wipe the interior with a damp cloth. Soak racks in warm soapy water. Avoid harsh abrasives on the interior coating.

faq.q: Can I use foil or parchment?
faq.a: Usually yes, in moderation. Do not cover the whole tray or touch the elements. In an air fry mode, weigh parchment down.

finalTake: For most kitchens, Breville's BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is the one to buy. Choose the BOV845BSS Smart Oven Pro if you skip air fry, the BOV680BSS if space is tight, and the BOV450XL Mini if you only want the name at the lowest price. Weigh the Joule models only when the price is level.
